title: PPF for Minors: Can Parents Invest ₹3 Lakh Annually?
description: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) has an annual contribution limit of ₹1.5 lakh per financial year across all accounts held by an individual. This ₹1.5 lakh lim.

faq.q: What is the maximum I can invest in my child's PPF?
faq.a: The maximum amount you can invest in your minor child's PPF account is ₹1.5 lakh per financial year. This limit is cumulative for all contributions made to that specific minor's account, regardless of who makes them.

faq.q: Do both parents get separate limits for a minor's PPF?
faq.a: No, the ₹1.5 lakh annual limit applies to the minor's PPF account itself, not to each parent. The combined contributions from both parents (or any other individual) to the minor's PPF account cannot exceed ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year.

faq.q: What happens if I contribute more than ₹1.5 lakh to my child's PPF?
faq.a: Any amount contributed beyond the ₹1.5 lakh annual limit in a minor's PPF account will not earn interest and will not be eligible for tax benefits under Section 80C. The excess amount may be held without interest or returned by the bank/post office.

faq.q: Are contributions to a minor's PPF eligible for 80C deduction?
faq.a: Yes, contributions made to a minor's PPF account are eligible for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, up to the overall limit of ₹1.5 lakh per financial year. This deduction is claimed by the parent whose income the minor's income is clubbed with.

faq.q: When does a minor's PPF account mature?
faq.a: A minor's PPF account matures 15 years from the end of the financial year in which it was opened. Upon the minor attaining majority, the account holder can operate the account themselves.

faq.q: Can a grandparent contribute to a minor's PPF?
faq.a: Yes, a grandparent can contribute to a minor's PPF account. However, these contributions will also be counted towards the ₹1.5 lakh annual limit for that minor's account, and the clubbing provisions of income tax will still apply to the parents.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on a minor's PPF taxable?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on a minor's PPF account is tax-exempt, just like an adult's PPF account. While the income from the minor's account is clubbed with the parent's income, the EEE status of PPF ensures the interest remains tax-free.
